about: IGSP's own published measurements, one file per lane; the release summary's IGSP entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 3 November 2026 (version string 0.13.0) for every in-claim and out-of-claim fit
comparator: graphical-model-learning 0.1a8 (igsp) with conditional-independence 0.1a6 and graphical-models 0.1a21, the authors' library and the method's only implementation; in the 27 cells with a setting of two or more targets also a copy of it patched so that its I-contradicting test follows Definition 4.2 of Yang, Katcoff, and Uhler (2018) (benchmarks/patches/gml-igsp-def42.patch)

defaults.alpha_none: one over the number of observational rows, for both tests, as for ut_igsp: 1e-3 at n 1,000, 1e-4 at 10,000, and 1e-5 at 100,000 in the in-claim cells (one observational environment of n rows each)

rows.J2: Andrey at n_starts=10, its default, against the reference at nruns=5, the library's default, at the same alpha for both tests
rows.J1: Andrey at n_starts=5 against the same reference fits
rows.levels: alpha 1e-4, 1e-3 (Andrey's former default, equal to the default at 1,000 observational rows), 1e-2, within the authors' sweep; the library has no default level

data: andrey.data in the generator's own units (scale='raw'), columns in an order drawn from the seed; an observational environment and every setting of n rows each; blocks W and S follow Wang et al. (2017), Figures 2 and 3; Y5, Y6, and Y8 Yang et al. (2018), Figures 5, 6, and 8 (comparisons/igsp.md, Data)
fit_protocol: every package of a dataset in its own child process pinned to one core with one BLAS thread; 5 draws per dataset in claim (Andrey seed 0-4, the library's Python random and NumPy global generator seeded 0-4), one out of claim; a cap of 1,800 s per draw in claim and 3,600 s out of it, a draw over it a timeout, never scored
verdict_rule: per cell, row, level, and comparator: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, each the mean over 5 draws; side = where the 95% percentile bootstrap interval of mean D lies, read exactly (an end within 1e-12 of 0, floating-point residue of an exact 0, is read as 0; the gate read the ends as computed); worse = above 0 on seeds 0-19 and on a rerun on fresh seeds 100-119; better = below 0 on seeds 0-19 and on a rerun on fresh seeds (100-119, or 6000-6019 for J2 at alpha 1e-3); a row is judged only where the library beats the empty graph
error_metric: shd: variable pairs whose endpoint marks differ between the interventional essential graph of the returned DAG under the effective targets and the true one
residue_note: an interval end within 1e-12 of 0, floating-point residue of an exact 0, is read as 0, as the UT-IGSP lane reads it; residue lists every such end, on seeds 0-19 unless it names a rerun's seeds, and side_as_computed fields give the side where the reading changes it. The gate and the confirmation's scripts read the ends as computed, under which four verdicts differ: the W row (J1 alpha 1e-4 patched) is above 0 on seeds 0-19 and again on seeds 100-119, a replicated worse row, where read exactly it ties; the two Y8 inhibiting n 1,000 rows at alpha 1e-2 against the patched copy are lower with no rerun instead of tied; Y8 inhibiting n 10,000 at alpha 1e-3 with 10 starts against the library is below 0 on seeds 6000-6019, so better (11, not 10); and the confirmation counts 18 rows below 0 for alpha 1e-3 against 17, keeping 1e-3, where read exactly the two tie at 17 and the rule, written before any fit, gives the tie to one over the observational rows, the default
residue: Y8_inhibiting_p10_n10000 J2 alpha 1e-3 graphical-model-learning rerun seeds 6000-6019

replicated_row.status: read exactly, its interval on seeds 0-19 contains 0 (lower end 4.4e-17, residue of 0), so it ties and is not worse; read as computed it is above 0 there and on seeds 100-119, the campaign's one replicated worse row; the trace below gives the cause of its gap
replicated_row.cause: Andrey's first start is the minimum-degree order with its ties broken by its column ranks, the same in every draw, and a later start replaces its result only with a strictly lower objective; at alpha 1e-4 and 1,000 rows per setting the objective often ties the true DAG with a wrong one (the true DAG's objective equals the returned one's in 42 and 26 of 100 draws, and is strictly higher in 45 and 65), so where the first start lands on the worse member of a tie or in a worse basin the other four starts miss, all five draws repeat it, while the reference draws five fresh random starts per draw; draw luck adds to it; a smaller share comes from the reference's one-sided start test

evidence.i_contradicting_counts_agree: on every DAG traced: 200 of 200 returned DAGs, 80 of 80 true DAGs

null_target_arcs.what: true arcs out of a null target, summed over the 87 cells x 20 datasets as the mean over draws: reversed by the estimate, and all such arcs; Andrey at alpha 1e-3 and 10 starts

speed.ratio: per row, the median over datasets of Andrey's mean fit time over its draws divided by the reference's (alpha 1e-3, nruns 5); every fit on one pinned core with one BLAS thread, the two packages' fits of a dataset back to back on the same core

default_selection.seeds: 1000-1019, Andrey only, the 87 in-claim cells, one draw, no rerun: lower and higher mean the 95% interval of the paired mean difference below or above 0 on these seeds

confirmation.seeds: 6000-6019, 5 draws, against the reference at alpha 1e-3 and nruns 5 (and the patched copy in multi-target cells), 114 rows per candidate; the rule was written before any fit and chose among eligible candidates by the most rows below 0, a tie going to ainv_n_s10, one over the observational rows (one default rule for the two methods that share the engine)

candidates.ainv_n_s10: alpha None (one over the observational rows), 10 starts

confirmation.reading: ends read exactly, as in the rest of this file; the run's own verdict read them as computed: 18 rows below 0 for a0.001_s10 (one, Y8 inhibiting n 10,000 against the library, through an upper end of -2.2e-17) against 17, and it named a0.001_s10

same_level.what: ainv_n_s10 against the reference at its own level, one over the observational rows, nruns 5 (and the patched copy in multi-target cells), in the 50 cells at n 10,000 and 100,000; at n 1,000 this is the row above; never counted

vs_alpha_1e-3.what: ainv_n_s10 minus a0.001_s10, Andrey against Andrey on the same datasets, in the 50 cells at n 10,000 and 100,000; never counted
